newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's September vehicle output to show increase.
newsitem.headline: Japan's September vehicle output to show increase.

text.p: Japan's domestic vehicle production this month will show an increase from a year ago due to new models and stable exports, an official of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA) said on Wednesday.
JAMA earlier announced that domestic vehicle production declined 2.1 percent from a year earlier to 663,868 in August, the first year-on-year decline in two months.
Japanese vehicle output has been erratic this year, reflecting fluctuations in domestic sales and exports.

"Production this month will post a (year-on-year) gain as carmakers have to increase inventories of new models for domestic sale in the autumn, and their exports are expected to be steady," a JAMA official said. He said the export performance was helped by the weaker yen.
Five of a total of 11 Japanese automobile makers increased production in August, mainly because of strong demand for their new models.
JAMA estimated vehicle exports in August to have been flat compared with exports in August 1995. It will announce its official export figures for the month on September 27.
Industry sources estimated Japan's exports in August at around 261,000, up about 0.7 percent from the year before.

Toyota Motor Corp introduced new Carina and Windom sedans in August and Mark II, Chaser and Cresta sedans in early September. Nissan Motor launched its new Terrano Regulus sport-utility vehicle in August and the Stagea station wagon last Tuesday.
The JAMA official said full-scale output of new models such as the Mark II started in September.
In late August, Mazda Motor's Demio compact wagon, Mitsubishi Motor's Galant sedan and Legnum station wagon, and Daihatsu Motor's Pyzar compact wagon debuted in Japan.

Daihatsu's output in August rose a steep 12.8 percent from a year earlier to 34,277 units, mainly due to strong domestic demand for its Move mini recreational vehicle and partly because of output of the new Pyzar compact wagon.
A Daihatsu spokesman said the firm expected its output to continue to rise in September.
Toyota and Honda said they expected their domestic output to continue to rise in September because of robust demand for new models.

A Honda spokesman said it would increase output not only because of strong demand for its Step Wagon, CR-V, Orthia and Odyssey models but because it would start producing its new Logo compact car in September ahead of its launch on October 3.
